4264.new_note: *And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;* (Matthew 1:3). *And in those days Judah went to the house of Shem and took Tamar the daughter of Elam, the son of Shem, for a wife for his first born Er.* (Jasher 45:23). Matthew puts Thamar in the line of the Messiah (Christ), and Jasher tells where Yahudah (Judah) found her: in the house of Shem, the daughter of Elam the son of Shem. She is not a Canaanite brought in from outside; she is a daughter of Shem's own house, inside the kept line from Noah, and her sons Phares and Zara are of that seed on both sides. The women named in Matthew 1 are there to show the seed of promise being guarded, not strangers being added to it, and Jasher 45 is the witness that settles where Tamar came from.
4264.member_note: Jasher 45:23 — *took Tamar the daughter of Elam, the son of Shem, for a wife for his first born Er.* Jasher places Tamar in the house of Shem, so the Thamar of Matthew 1:3 is a daughter of the kept line, not a Canaanite.

The framework reads the four women as seed-preservation markers; Jasher 45 confirms Tamar's Shemitic lineage.

4280.new_note: *Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* (Matthew 2:16). *And the woman conceived and bare a daughter, and she called her name Miriam, because in those days the Egyptians had embittered the lives of the children of Israel.* (Jasher 67:3). Jasher tells the Egyptian slaughter in fuller detail than Exodus 1 gives it, and it counts from inside one family: Miriam is named for the bitterness of the days she was born into, and in the next verse Aaron is born as Pharaoh begins to spill the blood of the male children of Yashar'el (Israel). Herod at Bethlehem is the same hand in a later century, a king killing the infants of a town to reach one child. The kingdom of man always moves to kill the promised seed at its birth. It failed with Moses and it failed with Yahusha (Jesus).
4280.member_note: Jasher 67:3 — *the Egyptians had embittered the lives of the children of Israel.* Miriam named for the bitter days; Herod's Bethlehem is the same hand in a later century.
4280.old_note: *And the woman conceived and bare a daughter, and she called her name Miriam, because in those days the Egyptians had embittered the lives of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* Jasher 67 walks the Pharaoh-Mosheh-infant-slaughter narrative in fuller detail than Exodus 1 — the embittering of the children of Yashar'el, the spilling of male infant blood. The Herod-Yahusha slaughter at Matt 2:16 is the latest beat of the same antichrist-pattern.

4281.new_note: *Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* (Matthew 2:16). *And she conceived again and bare a son and she called his name Aaron, for in the days of her conception, Pharaoh began to spill the blood of the male children of Israel.* (Jasher 67:4). Jasher gives the decree a date: it began in the days Aaron was conceived, and the boy's own name carries it. Matthew gives Herod's decree a date too, from two years old and under, reckoned from the time the wise men told him. Pharaoh spilled the blood of the male children of Yashar'el (Israel) to keep a deliverer from rising; Herod slew the children of Bethlehem to keep the King from rising. Same fear, same answer, and in both cases the king's sword missed the one child it was sharpened for.
4281.member_note: Jasher 67:4 — *Pharaoh began to spill the blood of the male children of Israel.* The decree dated by Aaron's conception; Herod's decree at Bethlehem is the same move against the promised seed.
4281.old_note: *And she conceived again and bare a son and she called his name Aaron, for in the days of her conception, Pharaoh began to spill the blood of the male children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The Pharaoh-blood-of-male-children naming Jasher gives — *Pharaoh began to spill the blood of the male children.* Matthew 2:16's *slew all the children that were in Beth-lehem* is the Herod-version of the same line. Same pattern, two beats.

4282.new_note: *And when they were departed, behold, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.* (Matthew 2:13). *There was a man in the land of Egypt of the seed of Levi, whose name was Amram, the son of Kehath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.* (Jasher 67:1). Jasher 67 opens where the story of the deliverer begins, with his father, a man of the seed of Levi living in Egypt in the years when Pharaoh would begin to spill the blood of the male children. Matthew 2 opens the story of the greater deliverer the same way, with a father warned by the angel of Yahuah (the Lord) to carry the child into Egypt because a king is seeking to destroy him. Moses was hidden in Egypt from Pharaoh; Yahusha (Jesus) was hidden in Egypt from Herod. The kingdom of man always moves to kill the promised seed at its birth, and there is always a household ready to hide the child.
4282.member_note: Jasher 67:1 — *There was a man in the land of Egypt of the seed of Levi.* The deliverer's story opens with his father in Egypt, as Matthew 2:13 opens with Joseph carrying the child there.
4282.old_note: *There was a man in the land of Egypt of the seed of Levi, whose name was Amram, the son of Kehath, the son of Levi, the son of Yashar'el (Israel).* The Mosheh-parent narrative — Amram and Yochaved (Jochebed) — the deliverer-preserved-through-the-slaughter prototype. Matthew 2:13's angelic-Yoseph-flee-to-Egypt is the Messianic version of the same preservation pattern.

18217.new_note: *And Elohim (God) remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and Elohim (God) made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged;* (Genesis 8:1). *And a wind passed over the earth, and the waters were still and the ark rested.* (Jasher 6:33). Jasher stands almost word for word beside the Torah here, and it binds three things into one moment: the wind passes, the waters grow still, and the ark comes to rest. Genesis adds the cause the reader needs, that Elohim (God) remembered Noah, and that remembering is what sends the wind. The breath that moves over the deep and quiets it is the same breath that moved over the waters in the beginning; the flood ends the way the world began, with Elohim (God) ordering the deep by his Spirit.
18217.member_note: Jasher 6:33 — *And a wind passed over the earth, and the waters were still and the ark rested.* Jasher binds the wind, the stilling of the waters, and the resting of the ark into the one moment Genesis 8:1 describes.
18217.old_note: *And a wind passed over the earth, and the waters were still and the ark rested* (Jasher 6:33). The ruach passes over the deep and the chaos subsides, the same Spirit-over-the-waters that ordered the first creation now quieting the flood.

20237.new_note: *Behold, I spoke to you these twenty years back saying, Go forth from your land, from your birth-place and from your father's house, to the land which I have shown you to give it to you and to your children, for there in that land will I bless you, and make you a great nation, and make your name great, and in you shall the families of the earth be blessed* (Jasher 13:22–23). 28104.new_note: *And after that Yahudah (Judah) spake to Jacob, his father, and said to him: “Bend your bow, father, and send forth your arrows and cast down the adversary and slay the enemy; and may you have the power, for we shall not slay your brother, for he is such as you, and he is like you: let us give him (this) honour.”* (Jubilees 38:1). *Only teach your sons the bow and all the weapons of war, in order that they may fight the battles of their brother who will rule over his enemies.* (Jasher 56:9). In both books it is Yahudah (Judah) and the bow. Jubilees puts the bow in Jacob's own hand at Yahudah's (Judah's) urging while Jacob still lives, and names the enemy as Esau; Jasher puts the same charge on Jacob's deathbed, Yahudah (Judah) to teach his sons the bow and every weapon of war so that they can fight the battles of the brother who rules over his enemies, and the enemy who comes against that house before the chapter ends is Esau. Two tellings of one memory, that the tribe that reigns is the tribe taught to fight.
28104.member_note: Jasher 56:9 — *Only teach your sons the bow and all the weapons of war.* Jacob's deathbed charge to Yahudah (Judah), the bow against Esau's house that Jubilees 38:1 also remembers.

29126.new_note: *And all the sons of Adam assembled and came to Enoch that day; and all the kings of the earth with their princes and counsellors remained with him that day; and Enoch then taught the sons of men wisdom and knowledge, and gave them divine instruction; and he bade them serve Yahuah (the Lord) and walk in his ways all the days of their lives, and he continued to make peace amongst them.* (Jasher 3:31). *And on account of it Elohim (God) brought the waters of the flood upon all the land of Eden; for there he was set as a sign and that he should testify against all the children of men, that he should recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.* (Jubilees 4:24). Jubilees tells why Enoch was taken: he was set as a sign against all the children of men, to recount the deeds of every generation until the day of condemnation. Jasher shows him doing that very work on his last day among them, gathering the sons of Adam and the kings of the earth, teaching them wisdom and knowledge, and bidding them serve Yahuah (the Lord) and walk in his ways. The witness who will testify against the generations first pleaded with them to walk right while he was still in reach.
29126.member_note: Jasher 3:31 — *he bade them serve Yahuah (the Lord) and walk in his ways all the days of their lives.* Enoch's last day of teaching before he was taken is the witness Jubilees says he was set apart to bear.
29126.old_note: Jubilees 4:24 — *he was set as a sign and that he should testify against all the children of men, that he should recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.* the witness-to-the-generations role behind Jasher 3:31, where Enoch's last day teaching bids all men serve Yahuah and walk in his ways.

29159.new_note: *And it was after this that Yahuah (the Lord) said to Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me, on account of their evil deeds, and behold I will destroy the earth.* (Jasher 5:25). *And Elohim (God) said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.* (Genesis 6:13). Jasher carries the decree of Genesis nearly word for word: the end of all flesh is come before me, and behold I will destroy the earth. Where Genesis names the cause as violence filling the earth, Jasher names it as their evil deeds, and the two are one charge told by two witnesses. The same Yahuah (the Lord) who spoke to Noah speaks in both records, and the judgment on all flesh is settled before the ark is ever named.
29159.member_note: Jasher 5:25 — *The end of all flesh is come before me, on account of their evil deeds.* Jasher gives the decree of Genesis 6:13 to Noah nearly word for word before the command to build the ark.

29178.new_note: *And all the fountains of the deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened, and the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.* (Jasher 6:14). *And Yahuah (God) opened seven flood-gates of heaven, And the mouths of the fountains of the great deep, seven mouths in number.* (Jubilees 5:24). Both witnesses open the flood from above and from beneath at once. Jasher says the fountains of the deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened; Jubilees counts them, seven flood-gates of heaven and seven mouths of the great deep. The rain of forty days and forty nights in Jasher is the same water Jubilees watches Yahuah (God) release by his own hand, so the flood is not weather but judgment ordered from the throne.

29189.new_note: *And he said to them, Be fruitful and fill all the earth; become strong and increase abundantly in the earth and multiply in it.* (Jasher 6:42). *"And you, increase you and multiply upon the earth, and become many upon it, and be a blessing upon it. 29191.new_note: *And they went and returned every one to his way and to his place, and Noah and his sons dwelt in the land that Elohim had told them, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed Noah and his sons on their going out from the ark.* (Jasher 6:41). *And Yahuah (LORD) smelled a sweet savour; and Yahuah (LORD) said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake; for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more every thing living, as I have done.* (Genesis 8:21). Genesis records what Yahuah (LORD) said in his heart after the flood, that he would not again curse the ground nor again smite every living thing, and Jasher records what that mercy looked like on the ground: Noah and his sons dwelt where Elohim (God) told them, served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and were blessed by him on their going out from the ark. The promise never to repeat the flood and the blessing on the family that came out of it are one kindness, spoken over the same ground on the same day the ark was emptied.

29239.new_note: *And when all the wise men and conjurors went out from the house of Terah, they lifted up their eyes toward heaven that night to look at the stars, and they saw, and behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens, and he swallowed up the four stars from the four sides of the heavens.* (Jasher 8:2). *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,* (Matthew 2:1). On the night Abram is born, Nimrod's wise men look up from Terah's house and see one great star run across the heavens and swallow four others, and they understand its import; before the chapter is out Nimrod is demanding the child's life. On the night Yahusha (Jesus) is born, wise men from the east read the heavens the same way and come to Jerusalem, and Herod moves to kill the child. Twice the sky announces the seed of promise at its birth, and twice the kingdom of man answers by reaching for the infant. What happened to Abram is what happened to the Messiah (Christ), because it is one war against one seed.
29239.member_note: Jasher 8:2 — *behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens.* The star Nimrod's wise men read at Abram's birth is answered by the star Herod's wise men follow at the birth of Yahusha (Jesus).
29239.old_note: Matthew 2:1 — *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem.* The wise-men-from-the-east-at-a-royal-birth motif Jasher gives Abram is carried into the Messiah's nativity.

29504.new_note: *And Terah took his son Abram and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram, and all the souls of his household and went with them from Ur Casdim to go to the land of Canaan. And when they came as far as the land of Haran they remained there, for it was exceedingly good land for pasture, and of sufficient extent for those who accompanied them.* (Jasher 13:1). *Then came he out of the land of the Chaldæans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell.* (Acts 7:4). Stephen tells the route in one sentence, out of the land of the Chaldaeans, a stay in Charran, and then into the land after his father died, and Jasher walks it step by step: Terah takes Abram, Lot, and Sarai out of Ur Casdim meaning to reach Canaan, and the household stops in Haran because the pasture is good. Both witnesses agree that Haran was never the destination, only the pause, and that the call to Canaan was already in motion when Terah's household left Ur. Stephen tells in one sentence the journey Jasher tells step by step, and the two do not differ.
29504.member_note: Jasher 13:1 — *went with them from Ur Casdim to go to the land of Canaan.* Terah's household leaving Ur for Canaan and stopping in Haran is the route Stephen gives in Acts 7:4.
29504.old_note: Acts 7:4 — *Then came he out of the land of the Chaldæans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell* — the very Ur-Casdim-to-Haran-to-Canaan route Terah's household travels in Jasher 13:1.

29508.new_note: *And now therefore if you will hearken to my voice and keep my commandments, my statutes and my laws, then will I cause your enemies to fall before you, and I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will send my blessing upon all the works of your hands, and you shall lack nothing.* (Jasher 13:4). *And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.* (Genesis 15:5). Genesis gives the promise under the open sky: look toward heaven, count the stars, so shall your seed be. Jasher gives the same promise in Haran with its condition spoken out loud: if you will hearken to my voice and keep my commandments, my statutes and my laws, then I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven. The multiplying of the seed and the keeping of his ways are never two separate matters in the mouth of Yahuah (the Lord); the promise is sure, and it is walked in by obedience. What Genesis shows Abram believing, Jasher shows him being told to keep.
29508.member_note: Jasher 13:4 — *I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven.* The seed numbered like the stars in Genesis 15:5 is spoken in Jasher together with the call to keep his commandments.

29512.new_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Abram when he came to the land of Canaan, and said to him, This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever, and I will make your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* (Jasher 13:7). *And Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto Yahuah (LORD), who appeared unto him.* (Genesis 12:7). Both witnesses place the same word at the same spot: Abram arrives in Canaan, Yahuah (LORD) appears to him, and the land is given to his seed. Genesis says it in a line and then shows Abram building the altar; Jasher opens the word out, this land to you and to your seed after you forever, your seed like the stars of heaven, all the lands which you see for an inheritance, and then in its next verse Abram builds the same altar and calls on the same name. The gift of the land to the seed is spoken at the threshold, before Abram owns a single field in it.
29512.member_note: Jasher 13:7 — *This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever.* Yahuah (the Lord) appearing to Abram on his entry into Canaan and giving the land to his seed is the word of Genesis 12:7.
29512.old_note: Genesis 12:7 — *And Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto Yahuah (LORD), who appeared unto him* — the same land-to-your-seed word Yahuah speaks at Abram's entry into Canaan in Jasher 13:7.

29513.new_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Abram when he came to the land of Canaan, and said to him, This is the land which I gave to you and to your seed after you forever, and I will make your seed like the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* (Jasher 13:7). *For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.* (Genesis 13:15). Genesis 13 has Abram lift his eyes and hear that all the land he sees is given to him and to his seed forever, and Jasher gathers that same word into the first appearing at Abram's entry into Canaan: I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see. The measure of the gift is the reach of Abram's own eyes, and the term of it is forever. Two witnesses, one promise, and no later covenant takes back a yard of it.
29513.member_note: Jasher 13:7 — *I will give to your seed for an inheritance all the lands which you see.* All the land Abram sees given to his seed forever is the word of Genesis 13:15 spoken in Jasher at his entry into Canaan.
29513.old_note: Genesis 13:15 — *For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever* — the all-the-lands-which-you-see inheritance forever of Jasher 13:7.

29522.new_note: *Go forth from your land, from your birth-place and from your father’s house, to the land which I have shown you to give it to you and to your children, for there in that land will I bless you, and make you a great nation, and make your name great, and in you shall the families of the earth be blessed.* (Jasher 13:23). *And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.* (Genesis 12:3). Jasher has Yahuah (the Lord) remind Abram in Haran of what he said twenty years before, and the closing clause is the one Genesis preserves: in you shall the families of the earth be blessed. Jasher also keeps the going out from land and birth-place and father's house, the great nation, and the great name, so the whole call of Genesis 12 stands in this one verse. The blessing on the families of the earth runs through Abram and his seed; it is not spread out apart from them, it is carried by them.
29522.member_note: Jasher 13:23 — *in you shall the families of the earth be blessed.* The blessing on all families of the earth from Genesis 12:3 is kept in Jasher's recall of Abram's call in Haran.

29569.new_note: *And now therefore behold, here is all belonging to you, take it and go; as Yahuah (the Lord) lives I will not take from you from a living soul down to a shoetie or thread, excepting the expense of the food of those who went out with me to battle, as also the portions of the men who went with me, Anar, Ashcol, and Mamre, they and their men, as well as those also who had remained to watch the baggage, they shall take their portion of the spoil.* (Jasher 16:16). *And Abram said to him: “I lift up my hands to the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), that from a thread to a shoe-latchet I shall not take aught that is your, lest you should say I have made Abram rich; save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me–Aner, Eschol, and Mamre. These will take their portion.”* (Jubilees 13:29). Jubilees and Jasher give the same oath in nearly the same words. Abram will not take from Sodom's king so much as a thread or a shoe-latchet, Jubilees says, lest it be said that man made Abram rich; Jasher has him swear as Yahuah (the Lord) lives that he will take nothing from a living soul down to a shoetie or thread. Both keep the same exceptions, what the young men ate and the portions of Anar, Ashcol, and Mamre. Abram's riches had just been promised him by Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) in the verse before, and he would not let Sodom claim the credit.
29569.member_note: Jasher 16:16 — *I will not take from you from a living soul down to a shoetie or thread.* Abram's oath to take nothing of Sodom's spoil is the same thread and shoe-latchet refusal Jubilees 13:29 records.
29569.old_note: Jubilees 13:29 — *I lift up my hands to the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), that from a thread to a shoe-latchet I shall not take aught that is your, lest you should say I have made Abram rich; save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me–Aner, Eschol, and Mamre.* Jubilees renders Abram's refusal in Jasher 16:16 with the same thread-to-shoe-latchet oath.

29990.new_note: *And the child grew up and he was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast upon the day that Isaac was weaned.* (Jasher 21:4). *And the child grew, and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast the same day that Isaac was weaned.* (Genesis 21:8). Jasher retells the Genesis verse almost word for word: the child grew, he was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day of the weaning. Where Genesis stops, Jasher goes on in its next verse to name who came, Shem and Eber and the great people of the land and Abimelech with Phicol, so the feast of Isaac's weaning is a gathering of the kept line and the kings around it. The son of promise is celebrated in the open before all of them.
29990.member_note: Jasher 21:4 — *Abraham made a great feast upon the day that Isaac was weaned.* Jasher retells the great weaning feast of Genesis 21:8 and then names the guests who came to it.
29990.old_note: Genesis 21:8 — *And the child grew, and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast the same day that Isaac was weaned.* Jasher 21:4 retells the canon's great weaning feast verbatim in substance.

30027.new_note: Matthew 4:10 — *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God), and him only shalt thou serve.* As the adversary tempts Abraham aside from the command in Jasher 23:25, so the Messiah turns the same tempter away with the word — the chosen seed will not be drawn aside.

30529.new_note: *And she bare to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuach, being six sons. And the children of Zimran were Abihen, Molich and Narim.* (Jasher 25:2). *And Abraham took to himself a third wife, and her name was Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah.* (Jubilees 19:11). Jubilees records Abraham taking Keturah as a third wife after Hagar had died, and Jasher gives the six sons she bore him, Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuach, and then goes further into their children. The two records sit side by side on the same household in Abraham's old age. Jasher's naming of the grandsons shows how far the sons of Keturah spread, and Genesis will say Abraham gave them gifts and sent them away from Isaac, so the seed of promise and the other sons of Abraham are kept distinct from the start.
30529.member_note: Jasher 25:2 — *she bare to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuach, being six sons.* Keturah's six sons in Jasher stand beside Jubilees 19:11, which records Abraham taking her as his third wife.

And she bare him six sons, Zimram, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah, in the two weeks of years.* The same Keturah-and-six-sons scene in the parallel patriarchal record beside Jasher 25:2.

31322.new_note: Deuteronomy 11:25 — *There shall no man be able to stand before you: for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon, as he hath said unto you.* The dread Judah expects to fall on the Canaanite kings (Jasher 34:55) is the laid-on fear Moses promises the land.

31404.new_note: *And all the inhabitants of the city of Sarton were powerful men, one of them would pursue a thousand, and two of them would not flee from ten thousand of the rest of men.* (Jasher 38:50). *How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and Yahuah (LORD) had shut them up?* (Deuteronomy 32:30). Jasher measures the men of Sarton by the same yardstick Moses sings: one chasing a thousand, two standing against ten thousand. Yet the song asks how one could chase a thousand unless their Rock had sold them and Yahuah (LORD) had shut them up, and that is exactly what the next verse of Jasher shows, the sons of Jacob slaying those mighty men with the edge of the sword and no man standing against them. Strength that could rout a thousand fell in a day, because the hand that gives such strength can shut it up.
31404.member_note: Jasher 38:50 — *one of them would pursue a thousand, and two of them would not flee from ten thousand.* The one who chases a thousand in Deuteronomy 32:30 is the measure Jasher gives the men of Sarton before the sons of Jacob slay them.
31404.old_note: Deuteronomy 32:30 — *How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and Yahuah (LORD) had shut them up?* The Song of Moses names the same one-chasing-a-thousand measure of Jasher 38:50 and ties it to the Rock's hand, not mere strength.

31420.new_note: *And Judah took the swords which had fallen from their hands, and Judah fought with them and slew twenty of their men upon the wall.* (Jasher 39:34). *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee.* (Genesis 49:8). Jacob's blessing says Yahudah's (Judah's) hand shall be in the neck of his enemies, and Jasher shows what that looks like before the blessing is ever spoken: the men on the wall drop their swords at his shout, and Yahudah (Judah) takes up the fallen swords and slays twenty of them where they stand. The next verse of Jasher says Yahuah (the Lord) put the fear of Yahudah (Judah) in their hearts, so the hand on the enemy's neck is Yahuah's (the Lord's) doing through him. The lion of the blessing is already on the wall.
31420.member_note: Jasher 39:34 — *Judah took the swords which had fallen from their hands, and Judah fought with them.* Yahudah (Judah) slaying twenty men with their own fallen swords is the hand in the neck of his enemies that Genesis 49:8 foretells.
31420.old_note: Genesis 49:8 — *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee.* Judah seizing the fallen swords and slaying twenty upon the wall is the hand-on-the-enemies'-neck the blessing foretells.

32271.new_note: *And Joseph was afraid of her at her doing this thing, and he rose up to flee from her, and she seized the front of his garments, and in the terror of his flight the garment which Zelicah seized was torn, and Joseph left the garment in the hand of Zelicah, and he fled and got out, for he was in fear.* (Jasher 44:54). *But she embraced him and held him fast in the house in order to force him to lie with her, and closed the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands and broke through the door and fled without from her presence.* (Jubilees 39:9). Jubilees and Jasher keep the same ending to the same scene: the garment left in her hands and Joseph fleeing from her presence. Jubilees has her close the doors and hold him fast until he breaks through and runs; Jasher has her seize the front of his garments so that it tears in the terror of his flight. Both put the torn garment in her hand, which is the very thing she will turn into a false witness against him in the verses that follow. The evidence of his innocence becomes the tool of his accusation.
32271.member_note: Jasher 44:54 — *Joseph left the garment in the hand of Zelicah, and he fled and got out.* The garment left in Potiphar's wife's hand as Joseph flees is kept by Jubilees 39:9 as well.
32271.old_note: Jubilees 39:9 — *But she embraced him and held him fast in the house in order to force him to lie with her, and closed the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands and broke through the door and fled without from her presence.* The live Jubilees text holds the same garment-in-her-hands flight as Jasher 44:54.

32278.new_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.* (Jasher 44:12). *And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.* (Genesis 39:5). Jasher retells the Genesis verse in a sentence: Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph, he prospered, and the house of Potiphar was blessed for his sake. Genesis spells out the reach of it, upon all that Potiphar had in the house and in the field, from the day Joseph was made overseer. The blessing does not stop at the man Yahuah (the Lord) is with; it spills over onto the house that holds him, even the house of a stranger that holds him as a slave.
32278.member_note: Jasher 44:12 — *Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.* Jasher retells Genesis 39:5, where Potiphar's whole house is blessed for Joseph's sake.
32278.old_note: Genesis 39:5 — *And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.* The blessing-of-Potiphar's-house in Jasher 44:12 is this verse retold.

32317.new_note: *And Joseph said to him, The three baskets which you did see are three days, yet within three days Pharaoh will take off your head, and hang you upon a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from off you, as you saw in your dream.* (Jasher 46:14). *Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.* (Genesis 40:19). Joseph's verdict on the baker runs the same in both records: within three days Pharaoh will take his head, hang him on a tree, and the birds will eat his flesh. Jasher adds only the reading of the three baskets as three days, which Genesis gives in the verse before. The dream that promised the butler his place promised the baker a tree, and Joseph told each man the truth of his own dream without softening it.
32317.member_note: Jasher 46:14 — *within three days Pharaoh will take off your head, and hang you upon a tree.* Joseph's verdict that the baker will hang on a tree is the word of Genesis 40:19.
32317.old_note: Genesis 40:19 — *Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.* the hanging-on-a-tree verdict Joseph speaks in Jasher 46:14.

32342.new_note: *And Isaac called Jacob and his sons, and they all came and sat before Isaac, and Isaac said to Jacob, Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of the whole earth said to me, To your seed will I give this land for an inheritance if your children keep my statutes and my ways, and I will perform to them the oath which I swore to your father Abraham.* (Jasher 47:7). *Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;* (Genesis 26:3). The word Isaac passes to Jacob and his sons in Jasher is the word Yahuah (the Lord) first spoke to Isaac himself in Genesis: to your seed I will give this land, and I will perform the oath I swore to Abraham your father. Isaac does not hand it on as a bare deed; he hands it on with its condition in the open, if your children keep my statutes and my ways, and in the next verse he tells Jacob to teach his children and his children's children to fear Yahuah (the Lord). The land, the oath, and the keeping of his ways are passed down together from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob.
32342.member_note: Jasher 47:7 — *To your seed will I give this land for an inheritance if your children keep my statutes and my ways.* Isaac hands Jacob the land oath Yahuah (the Lord) spoke to him in Genesis 26:3, with the keeping of his statutes attached.
32342.old_note: Genesis 26:3 — *Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;* The land-for-the-seed oath Isaac repeats in Jasher 47:7 is the word Yahuah first spoke directly to him.

33311.new_note: *And Joseph did all these things, and made these statutes, in order that he might know when his brethren should come to Egypt to buy corn; and Joseph’s people caused it daily to be proclaimed in Egypt according to these words and statutes which Joseph had commanded.* (Jasher 50:37). *And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.* (Genesis 42:6). Jasher explains why Joseph set up his statutes for the sale of corn: so that he would know the moment his brethren came down to Egypt to buy. Genesis gives the moment itself, Joseph the governor selling to all the people of the land, and his brethren coming in and bowing before him with their faces to the earth. The sheaves of his boyhood dream bow at last, and Jasher shows it was not chance that brought them before him but a net Joseph had spread across all Egypt for that very day.
33311.member_note: Jasher 50:37 — *in order that he might know when his brethren should come to Egypt to buy corn.* Joseph's statutes for the corn sale are laid so that the bowing of his brethren in Genesis 42:6 comes before his own face.
33311.old_note: Genesis 42:6 — *And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.* Joseph's whole apparatus of statutes in Jasher 50:37 'that he might know when his brethren should come' culminates in this bowing — the dream fulfilled.

33412.new_note: *And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Place your father and brethren in the best part of the land, withhold not from them all that is good, and cause them to eat of the fat of the land.* (Jasher 55:22). *The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if thou knowest any men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.* (Genesis 47:6). Pharaoh's grant in Jasher is the decree Genesis records, and Joseph's answer in the next verse of Jasher names Goshen just as Pharaoh names it here. The best of the land is given to shepherds out of Canaan by the king of Egypt, and it is given because of Joseph. Yahuah (the Lord) had sent him ahead to keep the family alive, and now the family is settled on the fat of the land by the word of the very throne whose successors would enslave their children.
33412.member_note: Jasher 55:22 — *Place your father and brethren in the best part of the land.* Pharaoh's grant, the same decree as Genesis 47:6.
33412.old_note: Genesis 47:6 — *The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if thou knowest any men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.* Pharaoh's best-of-the-land grant in Jasher 55:22 is the same decree.

33414.new_note: *And Jacob said to Joseph, Now I will die cheerfully after I have seen your face, that you are still living and with glory.* (Jasher 55:16). *And Yashar'el (Israel) said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.* (Genesis 46:30). Jacob says the same thing in both books, and he says it for the same reason. The face he had mourned as dead is in front of him, alive and in glory, and there is nothing left for this life to give him. Genesis has him ready to die having seen it; Jasher has him die cheerfully. A father who has his son back has nothing more to ask.
33414.member_note: Jasher 55:16 — *Now I will die cheerfully after I have seen your face.* Jacob's word on seeing Joseph alive, the same word Genesis 46:30 gives him.
33414.old_note: Genesis 46:30 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.* Jacob's now-let-me-die in Jasher 55:16 is the same word — the father content having seen his living son.

33415.new_note: *And behold Jacob ran and hastened to his son Joseph and fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they wept, and Joseph also embraced his father and kissed him, and they wept and all the people of Egypt wept with them.* (Jasher 55:15). *And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Yashar'el (Israel) his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.* (Genesis 46:29). Jasher gives the meeting of Genesis in fuller motion: Jacob runs to Joseph and falls on his neck and kisses him, Joseph embraces and kisses his father, and all Egypt weeps with them. Genesis keeps the same falling on the neck and the long weeping, and adds the chariot made ready and the presenting of himself to Yashar'el (Israel) his father in Goshen. Twenty-two years of grief end on a neck in Goshen, and the next verse of Jasher gives Jacob's words, that now he can die cheerfully having seen Joseph's face.
33415.member_note: Jasher 55:15 — *Jacob ran and hastened to his son Joseph and fell upon his neck and kissed him.* Jacob falling on Joseph's neck in Jasher is the meeting in Goshen of Genesis 46:29.
33415.old_note: Genesis 46:29 — *And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Yashar'el (Israel) his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.* The fall-upon-the-neck embrace of Jasher 55:15 is Genesis verbatim in substance.

33417.new_note: *At that time Jacob commanded his sons and household to go to Egypt according to the word of Yahuah (the Lord) to him, and Jacob rose up with his sons and all his household, and he went out from the land of Canaan from Beersheba, with joy and gladness of heart, and they went to the land of Egypt.* (Jasher 55:5). *And Yashar’el (Israel) went into the country of Egypt, 2172 A M. into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.* (Jubilees 45:1). Jasher tells the going down: at the word of Yahuah (the Lord), Jacob rose with his sons and all his household and went out from Beersheba with joy and gladness of heart to the land of Egypt. Jubilees fixes the date of that same journey, the new moon of the fourth month in the year 2172, when Yashar'el (Israel) went into Goshen. One witness carries the heart of the old man leaving Canaan; the other carries the calendar, and together they set the beginning of the sojourn in Egypt on a day that can be counted.
33417.member_note: Jasher 55:5 — *he went out from the land of Canaan from Beersheba, with joy and gladness of heart.* Jacob's going down from Beersheba to Egypt is the journey Jubilees 45:1 dates to the new moon of the fourth month.
33417.old_note: Jubilees 45:1 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) went into the country of Egypt, 2172 A M. into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.* Jubilees dates the same going-out-from-Canaan that Jasher 55:5 narrates from Beersheba into Goshen.

33422.new_note: *And Jacob said to Joseph and to his sons, Behold I die, and the Elohim (God) of your ancestors will visit you, and bring you back to the land, which Yahuah (the Lord) sware to give to you and to your children after you, now therefore when I am dead, bury me in the cave which is in Machpelah in Hebron in the land of Canaan, near my ancestors.* (Jasher 56:3). *And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,* (Genesis 49:29). The charge is the same charge. Jacob will not be buried in Egypt; he binds his sons to carry him to the cave at Machpelah where his fathers already lie. Jasher adds what the dying man says before the charge, that Elohim (God) will visit them and bring them back to the land Yahuah (the Lord) swore to give. The burial is the first step of that return, the father going home ahead of the children.
33422.member_note: Jasher 56:3 — *bury me in the cave which is in Machpelah in Hebron.* Jacob's burial charge, with the promise that Elohim (God) will visit them and bring them back.
33422.old_note: Genesis 49:29 — *And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,* Jacob's charge to bury him at Machpelah in Jasher 56:3 is the Genesis charge verbatim in substance.

33442.new_note: *And it shall come to pass when you shall go after Elohim to serve him and will teach your children after you, and your children’s children, to know Yahuah (the Lord), then will Yahuah (the Lord) raise up to you and your children a servant from amongst your children, and Yahuah (the Lord) will deliver you through his hand from all affliction, and bring you out of Egypt and bring you back to the land of your fathers to inherit it securely.* (Jasher 56:21). *By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.* (Hebrews 11:22). Jacob dies foreseeing the bringing out of Egypt; Joseph dies foreseeing the same departing and gives commandment about his bones because of it. Hebrews counts Joseph's word as faith, and Jasher shows where the son heard it first: at his father's bed, hearing that Yahuah (the Lord) would raise up a servant from among their children and bring them back to the land of their fathers. Neither man saw it. Both died holding it.
33442.member_note: Jasher 56:21 — *bring you out of Egypt and bring you back to the land of your fathers.* Jacob foresees the departing Joseph will foretell over his bones in Hebrews 11:22.
33442.old_note: Hebrews 11:22 — *By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.* The bringing-out-of-Egypt Jacob foresees in Jasher 56:21 is the very departing Joseph foretold by faith over his bones.

34561.new_note: *And all the souls that went forth from the loins of Jacob, were seventy souls; these are they who came with Jacob their father to Egypt to dwell there: and Joseph and all his brethren dwelt securely in Egypt, and they ate of the best of Egypt all the days of the life of Joseph.* (Jasher 59:19). *And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt already.* (Exodus 1:5). Jasher closes its roll of the family with the same seventy souls Exodus opens with, counted the same way, from the loins of Jacob. The number is the seed of promise as it stood going down into Egypt, a household small enough to name one by one. Exodus turns the page and says they multiplied until the land was filled with them; Jasher ends the sentence with them eating of the best of Egypt all the days of Joseph. Both books want the reader to see how few they were before they became a people.
34561.member_note: Jasher 59:19 — *all the souls that went forth from the loins of Jacob, were seventy souls.* The seventy Exodus 1:5 counts, the household as it stood going down into Egypt.
34561.old_note: Exodus 1:5 — *And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt already.* Exodus echoes the same seventy-from-the-loins count that closes Jasher's roll in 59:19.

34609.new_note: *And this was also from Yahuah (the Lord), for the children of Israel, to benefit them in their latter days, in order that all the children of Israel might know Yahuah their Elohim (the Lord their God).* (Jasher 63:7). *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* (Genesis 50:20). Joseph said it of his brothers' betrayal, that they meant evil and Elohim (God) meant good; Jasher says the same of the bondage itself. The Egyptians embittered the lives of the sons of Jacob out of ingratitude, having forgotten who fed them in the famine, and yet Jasher names the affliction as being from Yahuah (the Lord), set for the good of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in their latter days. The purpose was that they would know him. Hard labor under a king who did not know Joseph was the ground in which a people learned the name of the Elohim (God) of their fathers.
34609.member_note: Jasher 63:7 — *to benefit them in their latter days.* The bondage itself named as from Yahuah (the Lord) and for their good, as Joseph said of his brothers' evil.
34609.old_note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* Joseph's evil-meant-for-good is the same reading Jasher 63:7 gives the bondage itself.

35908.new_note: *And the children of Esau sent to Pethor, which is upon the river, and they fetched from there a young man of beautiful eyes and comely aspect, whose name was Saul, and they made him king over them in the place of Samlah.* (Jasher 69:2). *And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.* (Genesis 36:37). The Torah's list of the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the children of Yashar'el (Israel) names the same Saul, from a city upon the river, succeeding the same Samlah. Genesis calls his city Rehoboth; Jasher calls it Pethor, and tells how the children of Esau went and fetched him, a young man chosen for his looks, and made him king. The two books agree on the man, the order, and the river, and Jasher supplies how he came to the throne.
35908.member_note: Jasher 69:2 — *they made him king over them in the place of Samlah.* The Saul of Genesis 36:37, from a city upon the river, and how the children of Esau fetched him.
35908.old_note: Genesis 36:37 — *And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.* The Torah's Edomite king-list names the same Saul-by-the-river succeeding the same Samlah that Jasher 69:2 records.

37330.new_note: *So Moses went forth from the land of Cush, and went home and ceased to reign over Cush, and Moses was sixty-six years old when he went out of the land of Cush, for the thing was from Yahuah (the Lord), for the period had arrived which he had appointed in the days of old, to bring forth Israel from the affliction of the children of Ham.* (Jasher 76:12). *Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.* (Acts 7:29). Stephen moves Moses from the flight out of Egypt straight to Midian; Jasher fills the years between with a reign over Cush that ends only when Moses is sixty-six and the appointed period has come. Both agree on the shape of the thing: a long stretch away from his brethren, a stranger, before the call. Jasher says why the Cush years end when they do, because the thing was from Yahuah (the Lord), who had fixed the time in the days of old to bring Yashar'el (Israel) out from the affliction of the children of Ham. The deliverer's waiting was on a schedule he did not set.
37330.member_note: Jasher 76:12 — *the period had arrived which he had appointed in the days of old.* The Cush years end on Yahuah's (the Lord's) schedule, the long stretch away from his brethren that Stephen names in Acts 7:29.
37330.old_note: Acts 7:29 — *Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.* Stephen frames the same long exile-before-the-call that Jasher fills with the Cush years, Moses a stranger far from his brethren until the appointed time.

37354.new_note: *And she conceived again and bare a son, but circumcised his foreskin, and called his name Eliezer, for Moses said, Because the Elohim (God) of my fathers was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.* (Jasher 78:10). *This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did Elohim (God) send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.* (Acts 7:35). Eliezer's name is Moses' own confession that the Elohim (God) of his fathers was his help and delivered him from the sword of Pharaoh. Stephen says the same of him from the other side: the man his brethren refused is the one Elohim (God) sent back as ruler and deliverer. The one delivered becomes the deliverer. Jasher has Moses name the rescue over his son in Midian, years before the bush, and Acts has the rescue become the sending.
37354.member_note: Jasher 78:10 — *the Elohim (God) of my fathers was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.* Eliezer's name confesses the rescue; Acts 7:35 has the rescued man sent back as deliverer.
37354.old_note: Acts 7:35 — *This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did Elohim (God) send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.* The deliverer-from-Pharaoh's-sword that Eliezer's name marks in Jasher 78:10.

37358.new_note: *And Zipporah conceived and bare a son and he called his name Gershom, for he said, I was a stranger in a foreign land; but he circumcised not his foreskin, at the command of Reuel his father-in-law.* (Jasher 78:9). *And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.* (Exodus 2:22). The naming of Gershom is the same in both books, nearly word for word: a stranger in a foreign land. Jasher adds something Exodus does not say here, that the boy was not circumcised, and gives the reason, Reuel's command to the son-in-law living under his roof. The next verse of Jasher has the second son circumcised and named for deliverance, so the two births mark the two halves of Moses' time in Midian, the stranger first and then the man Elohim (God) had helped.
37358.member_note: Jasher 78:9 — *he called his name Gershom, for he said, I was a stranger in a foreign land.* The naming Exodus 2:22 records, with Jasher adding that the boy was left uncircumcised at Reuel's command.
37358.old_note: Exodus 2:22 — *And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.* The same naming of Gershom that Jasher 78:9 records, the stranger-in-a-foreign-land confession word for word.

37388.new_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) sent by the hand of Aaron and turned all the waters of Egypt into blood, with all their streams and rivers.* (Jasher 80:3). *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the waters of Egypt, upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and that there may be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and in vessels of stone.* (Exodus 7:19). Jasher gives the first plague in one line and Exodus gives the command behind it, but both put the hand on Aaron. Yahuah (the Lord) sends by Aaron's hand, Aaron stretches out the rod, and every stream and river of Egypt turns to blood. Jasher's next verses follow the plague into the pitcher and the cup, which is what Exodus means by vessels of wood and vessels of stone. The plagues begin where Egypt drinks.
37388.member_note: Jasher 80:3 — *turned all the waters of Egypt into blood, with all their streams and rivers.* The first plague by Aaron's hand, as Exodus 7:19 commands it.
37388.old_note: Exodus 7:19 — *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the waters of Egypt, upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and that there may be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and in vessels of stone.* The blood-by-the-hand-of-Aaron of Jasher 80:3 is Exodus' own first plague.

37403.new_note: *And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry throughout Egypt in that night, for there was not a house in which there was not a corpse.* (Jasher 80:44). *And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.* (Exodus 12:30). Jasher 80:44 is Exodus 12:30 nearly word for word: the king rising in the night, the servants, all the Egyptians, the cry, and not a house without its dead. Jasher adds in the next verse that even the carved likenesses of the firstborn fell from the walls, so that the judgment reached the images as well as the sons. The night Yahuah (the Lord) passed through Egypt is told in both books with the same breath.
37403.member_note: Jasher 80:44 — *there was not a house in which there was not a corpse.* The night of the firstborn, Exodus 12:30 nearly word for word.
37403.old_note: Exodus 12:30 — *And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.* Pharaoh rising and the houseless-of-the-living of Jasher 80:44 is Exodus' great cry.

38877.new_note: *And Moses said to them, Fear not, stand still and see the salvation of Yahuah (the Lord) which He will effect this day for you.* (Jasher 81:28). *And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.* (Exodus 14:13). Moses' word at the sea is the same in both books: fear not, stand still, see the salvation of Yahuah (the Lord) which he will work this day. Jasher tells us whom he was answering. The people had broken into divisions, one resolved to throw itself into the sea, another to go back to Egypt, and the charge to stand still is spoken into that panic. Exodus adds the promise that the Egyptians they saw that day they would never see again.
38877.member_note: Jasher 81:28 — *Fear not, stand still and see the salvation of Yahuah (the Lord).* Moses' word at the sea, Exodus 14:13 spoken into a people split into divisions.
38877.old_note: Exodus 14:13 — *And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.* Moses' charge in Jasher 81:28 is the canon's stand-still word verbatim in substance.

38883.new_note: *Also a mixed multitude went up with them, and flocks and herds, even much cattle.* (Jasher 81:2). *And Yahuah (LORD) gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.* (Exodus 12:36). Jasher counts what went up out of Egypt with the children of Yashar'el (Israel): a mixed multitude, flocks and herds, much cattle. Exodus 12:36 adds what they carried, the things the Egyptians lent them when Yahuah (the Lord) gave the people favour in their sight. Together the two verses show a people leaving not as fugitives but as a nation going out with its wealth and its herds after the years of hard labor. The spoiling of Egypt and the cattle of Jasher are the same going out seen from two sides.
38883.member_note: Jasher 81:2 — *Also a mixed multitude went up with them, and flocks and herds, even much cattle.* What went up out of Egypt, beside the goods Exodus 12:36 says the Egyptians lent them.
38883.reason: Exodus 12:38 (the mixed multitude and the very much cattle) is the closer canon line to Jasher 81:2 than 12:36; the card is kept on 12:36 as given and the note joins the two as one going out.
38883.old_note: Exodus 12:36 — *And Yahuah (LORD) gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.* The substance carried out with the multitude of Jasher 81:2 is the canon's spoiling of Egypt.

38995.new_note: *And Moses finished commanding the children of Israel, and Yahuah (the Lord) said to him, saying, Go up to the Mount Abarim and die there, and be gathered to your people as Aaron your brother was gathered.* (Jasher 87:9). *And die in the mount whither thou goest up, and be gathered unto thy people; as Aaron thy brother died in mount Hor, and was gathered unto his people:* (Deuteronomy 32:50). Yahuah (the Lord) sends Moses up the mountain with the same words in both books: die there, be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered. Jasher compresses the Torah's longer speech into one sentence and keeps its shape. The man who led Yashar'el (Israel) out does not lead them in; he goes the way his brother went, and the people he leaves have just been given the whole law to walk by.
38995.member_note: Jasher 87:9 — *be gathered to your people as Aaron your brother was gathered.* The call to Abarim, Deuteronomy 32:50 in Jasher's wording.
38995.old_note: Deuteronomy 32:50 — *And die in the mount whither thou goest up, and be gathered unto thy people; as Aaron thy brother died in mount Hor, and was gathered unto his people.* Jasher 87:9 keeps the very gathered-to-your-people-as-Aaron wording.

38999.new_note: *Now therefore observe all the words of this law, and walk in the way of Yahuah your Elohim, turn not from the way which Yahuah (the Lord) has commanded you, either to the right or to the left.* (Jasher 87:6). *Ye shall observe to do therefore as Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.* (Deuteronomy 5:32). Jasher has Moses closing his life with the charge Deuteronomy records: observe all the words of this law, walk in the way Yahuah (the Lord) commanded, turn not to the right or the left. The two verses are the same instruction, and in both it comes with the whole law attached, not a part of it. The way is the commandments. To turn aside from them in either direction, adding or subtracting, is to leave the way, and that is the thing Moses forbids with his last words.
38999.member_note: Jasher 87:6 — *observe all the words of this law, and walk in the way of Yahuah your Elohim.* Moses' last charge, the Deuteronomy 5:32 word to keep the whole law and turn neither right nor left.
38999.old_note: Deuteronomy 5:32 — *Ye shall observe to do therefore as Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.* Jasher 87:6 repeats the very turn-not-to-the-right-or-left refrain of Moses' charge to keep the way.

39001.new_note: *And Moses said to Joshua, Be strong and courageous, for you will make the children of Israel inherit the land, and Yahuah (the Lord) will be with you, he will not leave you nor forsake you, be not afraid nor disheartened.* (Jasher 87:4). *Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.* (Hebrews 13:5). Moses gives Joshua the promise as he hands him the people: Yahuah (the Lord) will be with you, he will not leave you nor forsake you. Hebrews quotes that same promise to its readers as a thing he has said, and builds contentment on it. The word spoken at the edge of the land to the man who would lead Yashar'el (Israel) into it is the word still standing for the scattered children centuries later. Nothing between Moses and Hebrews withdrew it. It is the same mouth and the same promise.
39001.member_note: Jasher 87:4 — *he will not leave you nor forsake you.* The promise to Joshua that Hebrews 13:5 still quotes as his word.
39001.old_note: Hebrews 13:5 — *Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.* The New Covenant carries forward the very I-will-not-forsake-thee promise spoken in Jasher 87:4.

39010.new_note: *Rise up and pass the Jordan to the land which I have given to the children of Israel, and you shall make the children of Israel inherit the land.* (Jasher 88:2). *Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Joshua 1:2). The command to Joshua is the same command. Moses is dead, the people are on the east bank, and Yahuah (the Lord) tells the new leader to rise, cross the Jordan, and bring the children of Yashar'el (Israel) into the land already given. Jasher adds the charge that Joshua will make them inherit it, the very thing Moses had told him in Jasher 87:4. The gift was spoken before the crossing; the crossing is the people walking into what was already theirs.
39010.member_note: Jasher 88:2 — *Rise up and pass the Jordan to the land which I have given.* The commission of Joshua 1:2, with the charge to make the children inherit it.
39010.old_note: Joshua 1:2 — *Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The command to rise and pass the Jordan to inherit the land in Jasher 88:2 is Joshua 1:2 verbatim in substance.

39011.new_note: *Every place upon which the sole of your feet shall tread shall belong to you, from the wilderness of Lebanon to the great river the river of Perath shall be your boundary.* (Jasher 88:3). *Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be.* (Deuteronomy 11:24). The boundary Yahuah (the Lord) gives Joshua is the boundary Moses had already announced in Deuteronomy: every place the sole of the foot treads, from the wilderness and Lebanon to the great river. Jasher calls that river by its Hebrew name, Perath, which is the Euphrates. The word to Joshua repeats the word through Moses because the land was promised before either of them, sworn to the fathers, and each generation hears the same borders read back to it.
39011.member_note: Jasher 88:3 — *Every place upon which the sole of your feet shall tread shall belong to you.* The borders Moses had already read out in Deuteronomy 11:24, Perath being the Euphrates.
39011.old_note: Deuteronomy 11:24 — *Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be.* The sole-of-the-foot boundary to Lebanon and the river of Perath in Jasher 88:3 is the inheritance-word Moses already gave.

39015.new_note: *And the people went up from Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and they encamped in Gilgal at the eastern corner of Jericho.* (Jasher 88:10). *And the people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho.* (Joshua 4:19). Jasher and Joshua agree to the day and the place: the tenth day of the first month, the camp at Gilgal on the east side of Jericho. The tenth of the first month is the day the Torah sets for taking the Passover lamb, and the next verse of Jasher has them keeping the Passover at Gilgal on the fourteenth as it is written in the law of Moses. The people enter the land on the lamb's day and keep the feast four days later, forty years after the first Passover in Egypt.
39015.member_note: Jasher 88:10 — *on the tenth day of the first month, and they encamped in Gilgal.* The day and place of Joshua 4:19, the lamb's day, with Passover kept four days on.
39015.old_note: Joshua 4:19 — *And the people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho.* The tenth-day-of-the-first-month encampment at Gilgal in Jasher 88:10 matches the canon to the day and the place.

39074.new_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) gave the land to the Israelites, and they possessed it as Yahuah (the Lord) had spoken to them, and as Yahuah (the Lord) had sworn to their ancestors.* (Jasher 90:24). *And Yahuah (LORD) gave unto Yashar'el (Israel) all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein.* (Joshua 21:43). Both books close the conquest with the same sentence: Yahuah (the Lord) gave the land, as he had sworn to the fathers, and Yashar'el (Israel) possessed it. Jasher's next verse goes on as Joshua 21 does, rest from every enemy and not one word failing of all the good he had spoken. The giving is his; the possessing is theirs; and the oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob is the reason for both.
39074.member_note: Jasher 90:24 — *they possessed it as Yahuah (the Lord) had spoken to them.* The close of the conquest as Joshua 21:43 gives it, the land given as sworn to the fathers.
39074.old_note: Joshua 21:43 — *And Yahuah (LORD) gave unto Yashar'el (Israel) all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein.* The sworn-to-the-fathers land-gift that Jasher 90:24 restates as Yahuah giving and Israel possessing.

39080.new_note: *These are the inheritances which Elazer the priest and Joshua the son of Nun and the heads of the fathers of the tribes portioned out to the children of Israel by lot in Shiloh, before Yahuah (the Lord), at the door of the tabernacle, and they left off dividing the land.* (Jasher 90:23). *And these are the countries which the children of Yashar'el (Israel) inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), distributed for inheritance to them.* (Joshua 14:1). The same three parties divide the land in both books: Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes, and they do it by lot. Jasher sets the scene more closely, at Shiloh, before Yahuah (the Lord), at the door of the tabernacle, so that the inheritance of every tribe is portioned out in his presence rather than by the strength of any man's hand. Joshua 14:1 is the heading of the record; Jasher 90:23 is its close.
39080.member_note: Jasher 90:23 — *portioned out to the children of Israel by lot in Shiloh.* The division Joshua 14:1 heads, done before Yahuah (the Lord) at the tabernacle door.
39080.reason: Live Jasher text spells the priest "Elazer" where Joshua has "Eleazar"; quoted as it stands, in case the author wants the Jasher spelling normalized.
39080.old_note: Joshua 14:1 — *And these are the countries which the children of Yashar'el (Israel) inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), distributed for inheritance to them.* The same Eleazar-Joshua-tribal-heads portioning by lot that Jasher 90:23 records at Shiloh.

49945.new_note: *But go to my land and to my birthplace, and take from there a wife for my son, and Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) of Heaven and earth who took me from my father's house... he will send his angel before you and prosper your way, that you may obtain a wife for my son from my family and from my father's house* (Jasher 24:31). The restored witness keeps the second half of the charge — *go to my land and to my birthplace, and take from there a wife for my son* — the very *go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac* (Genesis 24:4), the bride sought from the covenant family alone.
49945.reason: Card is right (24:31 is the charge to go to Abraham's land and birthplace); but the note's second quotation dropped 'from there' — live reads 'take from there a wife for my son'. Patched that quotation only.
49945.old_note: *But go to my land and to my birthplace, and take from there a wife for my son, and Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) of Heaven and earth who took me from my father's house... he will send his angel before you and prosper your way, that you may obtain a wife for my son from my family and from my father's house* (Jasher 24:31). The restored witness keeps the second half of the charge — *go to my land and to my birthplace, and take a wife for my son* — the very *go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac* (Genesis 24:4), the bride sought from the covenant family alone.

52821.new_note: *And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.* (Genesis 34:25). *And Simeon and Levi swore and said, As Yahuah (the Lord) lives, the Elohim (God) of the whole earth, by this time tomorrow, there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city.* (Jasher 34:23). Genesis gives the deed, Simeon and Levi taking each man his sword on the third day and slaying all the males, and Jasher gives the oath that stood behind it the day before: as Yahuah (the Lord) lives, by this time tomorrow there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city. The vow is total, and it is sworn in the name of the Elohim (God) of the whole earth, which makes the deed heavier, not lighter. Jacob was filled with wrath when he heard it, and on his deathbed he will curse their anger, so the record keeps their fierceness as a warning, never as a pattern.
52821.member_note: Jasher 34:23 — *by this time tomorrow, there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city.* The oath Simeon and Levi swear in Jasher is carried out in the slaughter of Genesis 34:25.
52821.old_note: *And Simeon and Levi swore and said, As Yahuah (the Lord) lives, the Elohim (God) of the whole earth, by this time tomorrow, there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city* (Jasher 34:23). The extended witness gives the oath behind the deed — *there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city* — that is carried out in *two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males* (Genesis 34:25). The vow is total destruction; the framework records the fierceness that Jacob will curse, never a pattern to follow.

53756.new_note: *And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.* (Genesis 39:5). *And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.* (Jasher 44:12). Genesis says the Egyptian's house was blessed for Joseph's sake, and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) lay on all he had in the house and in the field; Jasher keeps it whole in one line, Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph. The presence that went down with him into slavery did not wait for his freedom to start working. Where the one Yahuah (the Lord) favours dwells, the blessing overflows onto the house that holds him.
53756.member_note: Jasher 44:12 — *Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man.* Jasher keeps the blessing on Potiphar's house for Joseph's sake whole beside Genesis 39:5.
53756.old_note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph* (Jasher 44:12). The extended witness keeps the blessing-for-his-sake whole — *Yahuah blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph* — matching *Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had* (Genesis 39:5). Where the favoured of Yahuah dwells, the blessing overflows onto the house that holds him.

54994.new_note: *Now therefore rise up and go to the man, and take for him in your hands a present from what can be obtained in the land and bring it before him, and may El Shaddai (the Almighty God) give you mercy before him that he may send Benjamin and Simeon your brethren with you* (Jasher 52:23). The extended witness keeps Jacob's blessing word-for-heart with the canon — *may El Shaddai (the Almighty God) give you mercy before him* — echoing *And El Shaddai (God Almighty) give you mercy before the man* (Genesis 43:14); the father gives up the son and casts the outcome upon the mercy of El Shaddai.

The extended witness keeps Jacob's blessing word-for-heart with the canon — *may the El Shaddai (Almighty God) give you mercy before him* — echoing *And El Shaddai (God Almighty) give you mercy before the man* (Genesis 43:14); the father gives up the son and casts the outcome upon the mercy of El Shaddai.
